messages:
sylvia: quick RFC follow-up: proposing a lightweight "lease circuit-breaker" to protect the evict/renew path from storms that cause fragmentation and CPU spikes.

Problem: when many tenants rapidly renew leases or flood renew RPCs, we see renew QPS spikes that delay eviction decisions and increase compaction. Need a safety net.

Proposal: add a per-node circuit-breaker for renew traffic with three states: CLOSED (normal), THROTTLED (sample + rate-limit), OPEN (reject renews for short cooldown). We pair this with a conservative fallback: convert renew attempts during THROTTLED/OPEN to soft-extend hints instead of full token renewals.

Example knobs:
```
circuit: { max_qps: 5k, sample_pct: 10, open_cooldown_ms: 2000 }
```

tom: two quick asks: 1) how do we surface when a renew was downgraded? need telemetry; 2) what about per-tenant fairness while CB is open? don't want single noisy tenant to take down others.

vik: implement per-tenant sub-buckets. breaker trips global only if many tenants hit their bucket limits; otherwise throttle the offending tenant. Also add exponential backoff per-tenant.

infra-bot: note: add metrics: renew_accepted, renew_throttled, renew_rejected, cb_state, top_offenders.

sylvia: failure semantics: when renew rejected, runtime treats key as expirypending; evictor may reclaim sooner. We'll emit event with trace id so SDKs can surface warning.

alloc-bot: bench snapshot: cb_trial_1 => global renew qps reduced 72%, fragmentation delta -7%, tail-latency unchanged. Need long-run test.

tom: ok, landing plan: alpha runtime-only flag + telemetry, beta add per-tenant limits in Dedicated, then GA. I'll help with console alerts.

sylvia: thanks. I'll draft a 1-page arch note and schedule a short sync with infra.

vik: also propose a quick safety: if CB is open and tenant is Dedicated with SLA, allow an override path behind auth.

sylvia: noted. will include in doc.
